GenerateMoveStateMachine.rationale: Node-by-node against SlimedBerserker.cs:49-64. Four MoveStates with matching ids (VOMIT_ICHOR_MOVE / LEECHING_HUG_MOVE / SMOTHER_MOVE / FURIOUS_PUMMELING_MOVE) in one closed four-cycle. The C# wiring is written awkwardly -- moveState4 is created inside an assignment to moveState.FollowUpState (SlimedBerserker.cs:55) -- so it is worth spelling out: VOMIT -> PUMMELING (:55), PUMMELING -> LEECHING_HUG (:56), LEECHING_HUG -> SMOTHER (:57), SMOTHER -> VOMIT (:58), which is exactly slimed_berserker.py:47-50. INITIAL state VOMIT_ICHOR_MOVE (:63 vs :51). The registration list order differs between the sides and does not matter (monster_state_machine step 23: the list is a registration bag keyed by id, and no walk iterates it). No branch state, so no AddBranch integer and no MonsterAi draw. Intents match: StatusIntent(10) -> STATUS_CARD; DebuffIntent + BuffIntent -> DEBUFF also=(BUFF,); SingleAttackIntent(30) -> ATTACK 30; MultiAttackIntent(4, 4) -> ATTACK damage=4 hits=4.

guards.rationale: PummelingDamage GetValueIfAscension(DeadlyEnemies, 5, 4) -> 4 with WithHitCount(4) (and `_pummelingRepeat = 4` at SlimedBerserker.cs:23 agrees) = _PUMMELING_DMG 4 x _PUMMELING_HITS 4; SmotherDamage (..., 33, 30) -> 30 = _SMOTHER_DMG; VomitIchor adds 10 Slimed to the DISCARD (`_vomitSlimeInDiscard = 10` at :27 agrees) = _VOMIT_SLIME 10; LeechingHug applies WeakPower 3m to the targets then StrengthPower 3m to itself = _LEECHING_WEAK 3 / _LEECHING_STR 3, in that order on both sides. All match slimed_berserker.py:13-18. The unused `_leechingDrain = 3` const (SlimedBerserker.cs:25) is dead in the source -- nothing reads it -- so its absence from the port is correct.

guards.what: LeechingHugMove passes a NULL applier for the Weak but the CREATURE for the Strength (SlimedBerserker.cs:77-78); the sim omits both (slimed_berserker.py:65-66)
guards.rationale: PROMPT.md class 15's shape -- paired applications rarely carry the same guard set, and here the source itself is asymmetric: `PowerCmd.Apply<WeakPower>(ctx, targets, 3m, null, null)` has a null applier while `PowerCmd.Apply<StrengthPower>(ctx, Creature, 3m, Creature, null)` names the Berserker. The sim's PowerCmd.apply defaults applier to None (cmds.py) and neither call passes one, so the Weak matches the source exactly and only the Strength differs. Same observable, established by execution rather than assumed and identical to monster/stabbot's guard (governing rule 3): the only four sim sites where `applier` changes an outcome are relics/unsettling_lamp.py:47, powers.py:195 (RitualPower), powers.py:1167 (ViciousPower) and powers.py:3094, and a monster self-buff gives the same answer at all four whether the applier is None or the monster. Concrete trigger: any ported listener branching on `applier is None`, or a power on the monster whose behaviour keys on which creature buffed it.

C# is `CardPileCmd.AddToCombatAndPreview<Slimed>(targets, PileType.Discard, 10, null)` at the default CardPilePosition.Bottom; the sim loops CardPileCmd.add_to_discard ten times, which appends (cmds.py:471). No random position is involved on either side -- contrast Noisebot's draw-pile add, which IS CardPilePosition.Random and does burn a Shuffle draw -- so this move consumes no entropy on either side. C#'s `if (player.Creature.IsDead) return` guard (CardPileCmd.cs:1008-1011) has no sim analogue but no observable either, since a dead player ends the combat before any reader sees the pile.
